title: What It Really Costs to Own a Ferrari Enzo

scenes.text: A Ferrari Enzo costs about three point six million dollars to buy, according to Hagerty. But what does it really cost to own one? Not what the internet guesses, but what our sources can actually support. This video separates the numbers that come with a source from the ones that do not, builds a labelled scenario, and shows where nobody has the data.
scenes.caption: WHAT IT REALLY COSTS TO OWN A FERRARI ENZO

scenes.text: Our sources are Hagerty's valuation page, Sports Car Market, RM Sotheby's catalogue pages, Wikipedia, evo, The Drive, a PistonHeads listing and the Italian site Italpassion. We also quote one website, Gearshifters, whose figures have no sources, and we mark them as unverified. Our own arithmetic is always labelled.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: HAGERTY · SPORTS CAR MARKET · RM SOTHEBY'S · WIKIPEDIA · EVO · THE DRIVE · PISTONHEADS UK LISTING · ITALPASSION · GEARSHIFTERS (UNSOURCED, FLAGGED) · EIA · US CENSUS

scenes.text: Start with the purchase. Hagerty's valuation page for a two thousand three Enzo shows three million six hundred thousand dollars as the value of a good car, with no change over twelve months. It counts sixty-six sales of two thousand two to two thousand four Enzos on record, and six public auction sales of the two thousand three model in the last three years.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY (2003 ENZO): #3 'GOOD' $3,600,000 · 12-MONTH 0% · 66 SALES (2002–04 ENZO) · 6 PUBLIC AUCTION SALES OF THE 2003 MODEL IN 3 YEARS · #1, #2, #4 CONDITION VALUES NOT LISTED

scenes.text: The range is wide. Hagerty's three-year auction results run from two million one hundred eighty-one thousand to four million four hundred twenty-seven thousand. Its all-time figures run from eight hundred thirty thousand five hundred to four million five hundred ten thousand. The most recent sale it lists is two million eight hundred sixty thousand at Mecum on the sixteenth of August twenty twenty-four.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: 3-YEAR AUCTION LOW $2,181,539 / HIGH $4,427,297 · ALL-TIME (2002–04) LOW $830,500 / HIGH $4,510,000 · MOST RECENT $2,860,000 MECUM 16 AUG 2024

scenes.text: The Italian site Italpassion lists a higher figure: a record of six point oh five million dollars at Monterey in twenty fifteen, with recent sales of four to four and a half million. An RM Sotheby's page shows a two thousand four Enzo sold for one million eight hundred seventy thousand dollars in California in twenty fifteen. These sources conflict, and none explains why.
scenes.caption: ITALPASSION (RM PHOENIX, 23 JAN 2026): RECORD $6.05 M MONTEREY 2015; RECENT SALES $4–4.5 M · RM SOTHEBY'S CALIFORNIA 2015: 2004 ENZO $1,870,000 · HAGERTY MAX $4.51 M < $6.05 M → UNRESOLVED

scenes.text: For scale: the United States Census Bureau's median household income for twenty twenty-four was eighty-three thousand seven hundred thirty dollars. By our arithmetic, Hagerty's typical Enzo value is about forty-three years of that income. The Enzo's original list price, six hundred forty-three thousand three hundred thirty dollars, per Sports Car Market, was about seven and two-thirds years of it.
scenes.caption: CENSUS MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME 2024: $83,730 · 3,600,000 ÷ 83,730 = 43.0 YEARS · 643,330 ÷ 83,730 = 7.7 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC; ENZO'S LIST PRICE WAS IN 2003 MONEY)

scenes.text: When new, the Enzo's list price was six hundred forty-three thousand three hundred thirty dollars, according to Sports Car Market. Evo gives about four hundred twenty thousand pounds for two thousand two. By our arithmetic, Hagerty's three point six million is five point six times the American price. On the sales in our sources, the car has so far sold for far more than its list price.
scenes.caption: SCM: ENZO LIST $643,330 · EVO: c.£420,000 (2002) · 3,600,000 ÷ 643,330 = 5.6× (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SALES ABOVE LIST: AS SHOWN IN THIS VIDEO'S SOURCES · OPTIONS INCLUDED IN LIST?: NOT STATED
scenes.chapter: What it cost new, and what it did

scenes.text: In October twenty eighteen, Sports Car Market reported an Enzo selling at RM Sotheby's London for two million five hundred thirty thousand seven hundred seventy-four dollars, including the buyer's premium. It said the seller's gain was roughly one million dollars over the original purchase price, assuming he paid list. By our arithmetic, the gap between that sale and list is one point eight eight seven million.
scenes.caption: SCM (17 OCT 2018): $2,530,774 RM LONDON, 15 SEP 2018, INCL. BUYER'S PREMIUM · 'SELLER'S GAIN ROUGHLY $1,000,000' · 2,530,774 − 643,330 = $1,887,444 (OUR ARITHMETIC) → SCM'S 'ROUGHLY $1 M' DOES NOT MATCH ITS OWN LIST PRICE; REASON NOT GIVEN

scenes.text: That mismatch matters for anyone counting returns. The two numbers cannot both describe a car bought at six hundred forty-three thousand three hundred thirty and sold for two point five three million. Possibly the owner paid more than list, or the sale price includes fees the seller did not receive. The article does not say. So we do not use its million-dollar gain figure.
scenes.caption: SCM: GAIN ~$1 M vs ARITHMETIC GAP $1.89 M · POSSIBLE REASONS (OWNER PAID ABOVE LIST; PREMIUM PAID BY BUYER) = OUR SPECULATION, NOT STATED · FIGURE NOT USED

scenes.text: Sports Car Market also said then that Enzo prices seldom sell under two million and top out just below three million, and that the new owner would not do nearly as well as the seller. The magazine gave the car an investment grade of B. By our arithmetic, Hagerty's typical value today is forty-two percent above that 2018 sale, so the magazine's caution has not yet proved right.
scenes.caption: SCM (2018): 'SELDOM SELL UNDER $2,000,000 AND TOP OUT JUST BELOW $3,000,000'; 'THE NEW OWNER WILL NOT DO NEARLY AS WELL'; INVESTMENT GRADE B · 3,600,000 ÷ 2,530,774 = +42.2% (OUR ARITHMETIC; HAGERTY'S TYPICAL VALUE vs ONE SALE)

scenes.text: Auction prices usually include a buyer's premium. The SCM sale price of two million five hundred thirty thousand seven hundred seventy-four dollars is stated to include it, while the RM Sotheby's catalogue pages we read give hammer-style results without saying. By our arithmetic, a one percent difference on a three point six million car is thirty-six thousand dollars, so the basis matters.
scenes.caption: SCM: $2,530,774 'INCLUDING BUYER'S PREMIUM' · RM SOTHEBY'S CATALOGUE RESULTS: PREMIUM STATUS NOT STATED · 1% OF $3.6 M = $36,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC; THE ACTUAL PREMIUM RATE IS NOT IN OUR SOURCES)

scenes.text: Compliance can cost too. The RM Sotheby's page for a two thousand four Enzo describes a factory European-specification car converted in California to meet state emissions, federal transport and smog rules, and legal to register in all fifty states. It does not say what that conversion cost.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (CA15): EUROPEAN-SPEC CAR CONVERTED IN CALIFORNIA (EPA, DOT, SMOG); 'LEGAL FOR REGISTRATION IN ALL 50 STATES' · CONVERSION COST: NOT STATED · US ALLOCATION: HAGERTY 80 vs ITALPASSION 111

scenes.text: There is also provenance. A UK Enzo listed on PistonHeads, one of thirty-one in Britain, records a Ferrari Classiche inspection in September two thousand fifteen, followed by certification. Our sources do not price the inspection, and the listing's own asking price is on application only.
scenes.caption: PISTONHEADS LISTING (2003 ENZO): CLASSICHE INSPECTION SEP 2015, CERTIFIED SHORTLY AFTER · COST OF INSPECTION: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · ASKING PRICE: 'POA'

scenes.text: Some context for the purchase price. The Manual listed the cheapest new Ferrari, the Roma, at two hundred forty-seven thousand three hundred eight dollars in October twenty twenty-four. By our arithmetic, a typical Enzo costs fourteen and a half Romas, or six point two of the most expensive standard Ferrari on that list, the SF90 Spider at five hundred eighty-three thousand nine hundred fifty.
scenes.caption: THE MANUAL (9 OCT 2024): ROMA $247,308 · SF90 SPIDER $583,950 · 3,600,000 ÷ 247,308 = 14.6 · ÷ 583,950 = 6.2 (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: And in ordinary cars: Kelley Blue Book put the average new vehicle price at fifty thousand eighty-nine dollars in August twenty twenty-six. By our arithmetic, a typical Enzo costs about seventy-two average new cars. The spread of Hagerty's three-year auction results, from two million one hundred eighty-one thousand to four million four hundred twenty-seven thousand, is itself two point two million dollars.
scenes.caption: KBB AVERAGE NEW-VEHICLE PRICE AUG 2026: $50,089 · 3,600,000 ÷ 50,089 = 71.9 · HAGERTY 3-YEAR RANGE: 4,427,297 − 2,181,539 = $2,245,758 (2.03×) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, per horsepower, a typical Enzo costs about fifty-four hundred dollars at Hagerty's value and its six hundred sixty metric horsepower. When new, it was nine hundred seventy-five dollars per horsepower at the list price. The F50 at Hagerty's three million six hundred fifty thousand and five hundred twenty horsepower is seven thousand nineteen dollars per horsepower.
scenes.caption: 3,600,000 ÷ 660 PS = $5,455/PS · 643,330 ÷ 660 = $975/PS · 3,650,000 ÷ 520 = $7,019/PS (OUR ARITHMETIC; PS = METRIC HP; FIGURES FROM WIKIPEDIA, HAGERTY, SCM)

scenes.text: How fast has the value grown? By our arithmetic, from the two thousand three list price of six hundred forty-three thousand to Hagerty's three point six million is a nominal rise of about seven point eight percent a year over twenty-three years. From the two thousand eighteen London sale to today, it is about four and a half percent a year over eight years.
scenes.caption: 643,330 → 3,600,000 = 5.6× OVER ~23 YEARS (2003 → 2026) = 7.8%/YR · 2,530,774 → 3,600,000 = 1.42× OVER 8 YEARS = 4.5%/YR (OUR ARITHMETIC, NOMINAL, BEFORE COSTS OR INFLATION) · START POINT FOR 2003 = LIST, NOT A SALE

scenes.text: Between list and the twenty eighteen sale, the same maths gives nine and a half percent a year, over fifteen years. So the pace has slowed, from nearly ten percent to four and a half. Sports Car Market said the Enzo was stable. Hagerty's current twelve-month change is zero. That is data, not a forecast, and it shows how little of the Enzo's gain remains for a new buyer.
scenes.caption: 643,330 → 2,530,774 = 3.93× OVER 15 YEARS = 9.6%/YR (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SCM: 'PRICES HAVE BEEN STABLE' · HAGERTY 12-MONTH 0% · 'LITTLE GAIN REMAINS' = OUR OPINION

scenes.text: The market is also thin. Hagerty counts only six public auction sales of the two thousand three model in three years, and sixty-six sales of two thousand two to two thousand four Enzos on record. By our arithmetic, that is two public sales a year. A thin market means that selling takes patience and that a single result can move the average.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: 6 PUBLIC AUCTION SALES (2003 MODEL, 3 YEARS) = 2/YEAR (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 66 SALES ON RECORD (2002–04 ENZO) · 'SINGLE RESULT MOVES AVERAGE' = OUR INFERENCE

scenes.text: There is also the cost of time. Our sources do not give interest rates or the cost of money, so we cannot say what three point six million dollars would earn elsewhere. That is a real cost of owning an Enzo, and probably the largest one, but we cannot put a number on it from these sources. We prefer to say so than to pretend.
scenes.caption: COST OF CAPITAL / INTEREST RATES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES · 'PROBABLY THE LARGEST COST' = OUR OPINION, NOT A MEASURED FACT

scenes.text: Finally, a note on the mileage. The UK Enzo in our sources covered about four hundred sixty kilometres during its current ownership, per its listing, while the car in the RM Sotheby's Phoenix catalogue has seven hundred forty-six miles in total. Both cars have been driven very little. If that is typical, maintenance would come from age rather than miles, a point our sources hint at but do not state.
scenes.caption: PISTONHEADS LISTING: ~460 KM DURING CURRENT OWNERSHIP · ITALPASSION: CHASSIS 128797, 746 MI · 'IF TYPICAL, AGE NOT MILES' = OUR INFERENCE, NOT STATED

scenes.text: Now the costs that have a source. Sports Car Market says an Enzo tune-up starts at three thousand dollars. It also reports that the car it covered, the two thousand eighteen London sale, had a sixteen-thousand-dollar service. The sources do not say what the service included. By our arithmetic, that service cost five times the starting tune-up.
scenes.caption: SCM (2018): TUNE-UP STARTS AT $3,000 · $16,000 SERVICE ON THE SALE CAR (SCOPE NOT STATED) · 16,000 ÷ 3,000 = 5.3× (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: A UK Enzo shows what a service history looks like. The listing says it had its first annual service in May two thousand four, at forty-nine hundred kilometres, and a service in July twenty eighteen at seventeen thousand fifty-four kilometres that included a clutch replacement, cam cover gaskets and four new Bridgestone tyres. The listing gives no prices for any of this work.
scenes.caption: PISTONHEADS LISTING: 1ST SERVICE MAY 2004 @ 4,900 KM · JULY 2018 @ 17,054 KM — CLUTCH REPLACEMENT, CAM COVER GASKETS, 4 BRIDGESTONE POTENZA TYRES · PRICES: NOT STATED

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, that car covered about twelve thousand kilometres between those two services, over fourteen years. So its clutch was replaced at roughly seventeen thousand kilometres, or about ten thousand six hundred miles. That is the only clutch data point for the Enzo in our sources, and it comes from one car, so it cannot tell us how long a typical clutch lasts.
scenes.caption: 17,054 KM × 0.6214 = 10,597 MI · 17,054 − 4,900 = 12,154 KM IN ~14 YEARS (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SAMPLE SIZE = 1 CAR · CLUTCH LIFE IN GENERAL: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The Enzo's gearbox is a first-generation automated manual, as Wikipedia's page notes, with complaints about abrupt shifting. The page does not discuss reliability or clutch wear. Evo's two thousand four test found the car remarkably tractable, comfortable and supple in town. Neither source gives a failure rate, so any claim of how often it needs a clutch has no support here.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: FIRST-GENERATION LATE-1990s CLUTCHLESS DESIGN; ABRUPT SHIFTING COMPLAINTS · EVO (FEB 2004): 'REMARKABLY TRACTABLE, COMFORTABLE AND SUPPLE' IN TOWN · FAILURE RATES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: A website, Gearshifters, publishes a list. It says an oil change costs about fourteen hundred dollars, a scheduled service close to nine thousand, a clutch assembly six thousand and a complete brake overhaul forty thousand, with insurance upwards of six thousand dollars a year. It cites no sources and gives no dates. The same article also refers to nine-thousand-dollar oil changes, which contradicts itself.
scenes.caption: GEARSHIFTERS (PUB. 2022-09-16): OIL CHANGE ~$1,400 · SCHEDULED SERVICE ~$9,000 · CLUTCH $6,000 · BRAKE OVERHAUL $40,000 · INSURANCE >$6,000/YR · NO SOURCES, NO DATES · ARTICLE ALSO REFERS TO '$9,000 OIL CHANGES' → INCONSISTENT · ALSO PRICE $650,000 vs $659,330

scenes.text: Treat that list as a rumour, not data. We include it only because anyone searching for Enzo costs will find it. Some of its figures are plausible next to our sourced ones; the nine-thousand-dollar service is about half the sixteen thousand reported by Sports Car Market, and the three-thousand-dollar tune-up is a different kind of job. But plausible is not proven.
scenes.caption: GEARSHIFTERS $9,000 SERVICE vs SCM $16,000 SERVICE: 9,000 ÷ 16,000 = 56% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SCOPES UNKNOWN · 'PLAUSIBLE ≠ PROVEN'

scenes.text: Let us build a scenario, labelled as ours. Imagine ten years of ownership, at one thousand miles a year, which is within the range of the low-use cars in our sources. Using only sourced figures, we assume one tune-up a year at the three thousand dollar starting price, and one sixteen thousand dollar service. This is an illustration, not a forecast.
scenes.caption: OUR SCENARIO (NOT A FORECAST): 10 YEARS · 1,000 MI/YEAR · 10 TUNE-UPS AT THE $3,000 'STARTING' PRICE (SCM) = $30,000 · 1 SERVICE AT $16,000 (SCM) · TUNE-UP PRICE IS A FLOOR (SCM: 'STARTS AT')

scenes.text: Add fuel. At about eight point one miles per gallon combined, from Wikipedia's twenty-nine litres per hundred kilometres, and the government's regular gasoline price of four dollars twenty-eight cents a gallon, ten thousand miles costs about five thousand three hundred dollars. The car's required fuel grade is not stated in our sources, so premium would cost more.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 29 L/100 KM COMBINED = 235.215 ÷ 29 = 8.11 MPG · EIA REGULAR $4.284/GAL (19 OCT 2026) · 10,000 ÷ 8.11 × 4.284 = $5,282 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · FUEL GRADE: NOT STATED → PREMIUM WOULD COST MORE

scenes.text: The total comes to about fifty-one thousand three hundred dollars over ten years, or roughly five thousand a year, by our arithmetic. Per mile, that is five dollars thirteen. It excludes insurance, storage, tyres, depreciation and the cost of money, none of which our sources price. Against a three point six million purchase, it is about one and a half percent.
scenes.caption: 30,000 + 16,000 + 5,282 = $51,282 · ÷ 10 YEARS = $5,128/YR · ÷ 10,000 MI = $5.13/MI · 51,282 ÷ 3,600,000 = 1.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · EXCLUDES INSURANCE, STORAGE, TYRES, DEPRECIATION, COST OF MONEY (NOT IN OUR SOURCES)

scenes.text: Now the pessimistic version, using the unverified website figures. Insurance of six thousand a year, a nine-thousand-dollar service each year, one six-thousand-dollar clutch, a forty-thousand-dollar brake overhaul and the same fuel gives about two hundred one thousand dollars over ten years, by our arithmetic, or twenty dollars a mile. That is almost four times the first scenario.
scenes.caption: UNSOURCED FIGURES: 10 × $6,000 INSURANCE + 10 × $9,000 SERVICE + $6,000 CLUTCH + $40,000 BRAKES + $5,282 FUEL = $201,282 · ÷ 10,000 MI = $20.13/MI · 201,282 ÷ 51,282 = 3.9× (OUR ARITHMETIC; INPUTS UNVERIFIED)

scenes.text: The truth lies somewhere in the range we cannot narrow. By our arithmetic, even the pessimistic scenario is less than six percent of the purchase price over ten years. The real cost of owning an Enzo is dominated by what happens to its value, and not by what it costs to run, as long as nothing breaks badly. That is also why the sourced numbers matter less than the price you pay.
scenes.caption: 201,282 ÷ 3,600,000 = 5.6% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'DOMINATED BY VALUE CHANGE' = OUR JUDGEMENT; 12-MONTH VALUE CHANGE 0% (HAGERTY) · 'AS LONG AS NOTHING BREAKS BADLY' = OUR CAVEAT

scenes.text: What if you drive it more? A heavier-use scenario, again ours. Say fifty thousand miles over ten years. At eight point one miles per gallon, fuel is about twenty-six thousand four hundred dollars. If the single clutch data point repeated, one clutch every ten thousand six hundred miles, that is four clutches, and at the website's unverified six thousand dollars each, twenty-four thousand.
scenes.caption: OUR SCENARIO: 50,000 MI IN 10 YEARS · 50,000 ÷ 8.11 × 4.284 = $26,413 FUEL · CLUTCH EVERY 10,597 MI (ONE CAR) → 50,000 ÷ 10,597 = 4.7 → 4 CLUTCHES · 4 × $6,000 (UNSOURCED, GEARSHIFTERS) = $24,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC; ALL INPUTS WEAK)

scenes.text: With the same thirty thousand in tune-ups and the sixteen thousand dollar service, the heavier-use total is about ninety-six thousand dollars, by our arithmetic, or one dollar ninety-three a mile. So driving the car five times as far lowers the cost per mile by almost two-thirds, but raises the total by about eighty-eight percent. Fixed costs dominate, as with most collector cars.
scenes.caption: 30,000 + 16,000 + 26,413 + 24,000 = $96,413 · ÷ 50,000 MI = $1.93/MI · vs $5.13/MI (−62%) · 96,413 ÷ 51,282 = +88% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'FIXED COSTS DOMINATE' = OUR JUDGEMENT FROM THIS SCENARIO ONLY

scenes.text: The biggest risk is a crash. RM Sotheby's says an alarming number of the four hundred Enzos have been written off by inexperienced or cavalier drivers. It gives no count and no repair costs. Our sources include no insurance claim data and no figure for repairing a carbon-fibre tub. So the cost of the worst case is simply not in our sources.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (CA15): 'AN ALARMING NUMBER' OF THE 400 'WRITTEN OFF' · COUNT: NOT GIVEN · REPAIR / INSURANCE-CLAIM COSTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: The next risk is rarity of parts and expertise. Wikipedia describes three development mules and the Maserati MC12, which shares the Enzo's engine, chassis and gearbox, with fifty cars built. Our sources do not say whether parts are shared with the MC12 in practice. So we cannot say whether owning an Enzo is easier or harder because of the sister car.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MC12 SHARES ENGINE, CHASSIS, GEARBOX WITH ENZO · 50 MC12 BUILT · PARTS SHARING IN PRACTICE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: A third risk is specialist labour. The Drive's article about the Ferrari F50, the Enzo's predecessor, says a clutch job needs the entire rear subframe and transaxle removed, with parts around five thousand dollars from a two thousand eight forum post. The Enzo has a different layout, and our sources do not describe its clutch access, so we only use this as a reminder, not as an Enzo figure.
scenes.caption: THE DRIVE (26 NOV 2019): F50 CLUTCH JOB — REAR SUBFRAME + TRANSAXLE REMOVED; PARTS ~$5,000 (2008 FORUM); EST. MINIMUM ~$7,000 · ENZO CLUTCH ACCESS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES → F50 DATA NOT AN ENZO FIGURE

scenes.text: The F50 also shows how big a service can be. An RM Sotheby's catalogue for a twenty twenty-one F50 lists work in August twenty seventeen, a new fuel bladder, tyres and brake lines, costing nearly fifty-one thousand dollars. The Drive quotes about eighteen thousand for the bladders alone from a forum. For the Enzo, our sources show a sixteen thousand dollar service. The scale is similar.
scenes.caption: RM SOTHEBY'S (F50, MONTEREY 2021): AUG 2017 BLADDER + TYRES + BRAKE LINES ≈ $51,000 · THE DRIVE: BLADDERS ~$18,000 (2010 FORUM) · SCM (ENZO): $16,000 SERVICE · 'SIMILAR SCALE' = OUR JUDGEMENT; SCOPES DIFFER

scenes.text: Selling is the other end. Italpassion reports that RM Sotheby's estimated an Enzo with only seven hundred forty-six miles at five to six million dollars in January twenty twenty-six. By our arithmetic, that estimate is between thirty-nine and sixty-seven percent above Hagerty's typical value, which reflects mileage and condition. We do not know the result of that sale.
scenes.caption: ITALPASSION (RM PHOENIX, 23 JAN 2026): ENZO CHASSIS 128797, 746 MI, ESTIMATE $5–6 M · 5 ÷ 3.6 = +38.9% · 6 ÷ 3.6 = +66.7% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · SALE RESULT: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Condition and mileage clearly matter. But Hagerty's own page lists only one condition price, the typical one at three point six million, and not the others. By our arithmetic, the gap between the auction estimate of the lowest-mileage car and the typical car is at least one point four million dollars, and our sources can't say how much of that is mileage, history or hype.
scenes.caption: HAGERTY: ONLY #3 'GOOD' PRICE SHOWN · 5,000,000 − 3,600,000 = $1,400,000 MINIMUM GAP (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BREAKDOWN OF GAP: NOT IN OUR SOURCES
scenes.orig_query: What a low odometer is worth

scenes.text: Also remember the mule. Wikipedia says the third development mule, dressed as a Ferrari three forty-eight, sold at auction in June two thousand five for one hundred ninety-five thousand five hundred euros, or two hundred thirty-six thousand three hundred dollars. By our arithmetic, that was thirty-seven percent of the Enzo's list price. Not every Enzo-related car has become a bargain at three million.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: MULE M3 SOLD JUNE 2005 FOR €195,500 (US$236,300) · 236,300 ÷ 643,330 = 36.7% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'DRESSED AS A 348' PER WIKIPEDIA (M1–M3 USED 348 BODYWORK)

scenes.text: And the Pope's Enzo, the four hundredth car, sold at Sotheby's for one point one million dollars, per Wikipedia, which also says the donation went to the Vatican while its own cited sources mention St. Jude Children's Research Hospital. By our arithmetic, that is thirty-one percent of today's Hagerty value. The sale was in the mid-two-thousands, our sources suggest, so it is not a comparable price.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: 400TH ENZO SOLD AT SOTHEBY'S $1.1 M · CITED SOURCES: ST. JUDE; DATED DEC 2005 · 1,100,000 ÷ 3,600,000 = 30.6% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · 'MID-2000s' = FROM THE DEC 2005 CITATION DATE; SALE DATE NOT STATED ON THE PAGE

scenes.text: Sports Car Market listed alternatives in twenty eighteen: the Bugatti Veyron, the Porsche nine eighteen and the McLaren P one. It gave no prices. Hagerty's Ferrari F50 page now shows three million six hundred fifty thousand dollars, only one point four percent more than the Enzo's, so for a buyer choosing between the two Ferraris, the purchase price gap is small.
scenes.caption: SCM (2018): ALTERNATIVES — BUGATTI VEYRON (2006–11), PORSCHE 918 (2013–15), MCLAREN P1 (2014–16) · NO PRICES GIVEN · HAGERTY F50 $3,650,000 (LABELS NOT SHOWN) vs ENZO $3,600,000 = +1.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: There are track-only cousins. The Ferrari FXX cost one point three million euros initially, per Wikipedia, and Ferrari kept the cars for client use. The Maserati MC12 Versione Corse sold twelve cars at one million euros each. Neither can be registered for the road. By our arithmetic, a road Enzo at three point six million costs about two point eight times the FXX's launch price in nominal euros and dollars, though currencies differ.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA: FXX €1.3 M INITIAL (2005), KEPT BY FERRARI FOR CLIENT USE · MC12 VERSIONE CORSE €1 M EACH (12 SOLD) · 3.6 ÷ 1.3 = 2.8 (OUR ARITHMETIC, MIXING $ AND € → ROUGH ONLY) · CURRENT FXX / MC12 VALUES: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: So what does an Enzo really cost? On our sources: about three point six million dollars to buy, a few thousand dollars a year to tune up, a service of around sixteen thousand dollars when needed, and fuel at about fifty-three dollars per hundred miles at the current price. The unsourced figures could be four times higher. Whether it really costs you money depends mostly on the price you pay and the price you sell for.
scenes.caption: BUY: ~$3.6 M (HAGERTY) · TUNE-UP FROM $3,000 · SERVICE $16,000 (SCM) · FUEL ~$52.82/100 MI (8.11 MPG × $4.284) (OUR ARITHMETIC) · UNSOURCED WEB FIGURES UP TO 3.9× OUR SOURCED SCENARIO

scenes.text: And the cost nobody can price from our sources is risk. Insurance, storage, tyres, damage, and the chance that the market turns. Hagerty's twelve-month change is zero, and Sports Car Market's twenty eighteen caution did not come true. But past stability is not a promise. We can tell you what the car has cost so far, not what it will.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: INSURANCE · STORAGE · TYRE PRICES · DAMAGE / REPAIR COSTS · COST OF MONEY · FUTURE VALUE · HAGERTY 12-MONTH 0% · SCM 2018 CAUTION NOT YET BORNE OUT (OUR OBSERVATION)

scenes.text: To recap what we could not confirm: insurance and storage costs, tyre prices, the buyer's premium rate on each sale, what the Classiche inspection costs, how long an Enzo clutch typically lasts, what a major repair costs, and why Hagerty's maximum is lower than Italpassion's record. Every one of those is flagged where it came up. If you own an Enzo and have real numbers, we would like to see them.
